title: A Study on Credit Default Prediction Using Hybrid AI Models Combining Neural Architectures and Econometric Features
venue: International Journal of Engineering Research and Emerging Technologies (IJERET), 6(2)
tldr: Proposes a hybrid AI model combining LSTM neural networks with logistic regression on econometric features (credit history, DTI ratio, employment status, loan purpose) for credit default prediction, achieving superior ROC-AUC (0.92 vs. 0.85 baseline) and low Type II error rate (7.8%).
problem_and_motivation: Conventional credit scoring models (logistic regression, decision trees) underperform on non-linear relationships, class imbalance (~5% defaults), and temporal dependencies in borrower histories. The credit industry is projected to grow to $2.1 trillion by 2025, yet default losses erode lender profitability. Prediction of credit defaults is a high-stakes problem where reducing False Negatives (approving a defaulting borrower) is critical for profitability.
approach: Hybrid architecture: LSTM (2 layers, 64 units) for temporal sequence learning from 24-month payment histories + logistic regression on static econometric features.
Data sourced from a financial institution's loan portfolio (2018-2023): ~200,000 borrowers, 78% performing loans, 22% default cases.
SMOTE oversampling for class imbalance; data split 80/20 train-test.
Feature engineering: 45 raw features reduced to 20 via PCA + correlation analysis (VIF < 5 threshold).
Training: Adam optimizer (lr=0.001), MSE loss, early stopping (patience=10), batch size 32, 100 epochs.
Threshold optimization using Youden's J statistic (optimal threshold = 0.32).
findings: Hybrid model achieves ROC-AUC of 0.92, significantly outperforming standalone LSTM (0.88) and logistic regression (0.85).
num: Sensitivity (True Positive Rate for defaults): 0.91 (hybrid) vs. 0.84 (LSTM) vs. 0.71 (logistic regression).
num: Specificity (True Negative Rate for performing loans): 0.87 (hybrid) vs. 0.82 (LSTM) vs. 0.78 (logistic regression).
num: Type II error rate (False Negatives): 7.8% (hybrid) vs. 12.5% (LSTM) vs. 18.2% (logistic regression).
num: Type I error rate (False Positives): 10.2% (hybrid) vs. 13.1% (LSTM) vs. 16.4% (logistic regression).
num: Most influential features: credit history length (SHAP importance: 0.21), DTI ratio (0.18), payment-to-income ratio (0.15).
Ablation study confirms that removing temporal features reduces AUC by 0.06, while removing econometric features reduces AUC by 0.08, confirming hybrid synergy.
Calibration analysis: Brier score = 0.09 (hybrid) versus 0.15 (LSTM) and 0.18 (logistic regression).
Computational efficiency: training time 1.76× longer than logistic regression but inference latency < 5ms per sample.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Demonstrates that hybridizing temporal (LSTM) and static (econometric) features yields superior default prediction accuracy and significantly lower False Negative rates than either component alone, with practical inference latency for real-time credit decisions.
directly_justifies: Supports Odin's credit risk scoring module by providing a proven hybrid architecture combining sequential payment history with static borrower features.
The SHAP-based feature importance approach can be replicated in Odin for explainable credit decisions.
Threshold optimization via Youden's J can be implemented in Odin's decision engine to balance lender risk vs. borrower approval rates.
limits: Single financial institution data source; may not generalize across different lending markets or regulatory environments.
No external validation on hold-out datasets from other institutions.
SMOTE may introduce synthetic samples that do not reflect real-world default patterns.
Fairness and bias analysis not addressed (e.g., protected attributes in lending decisions).
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Credit default prediction with hybrid AI model makes this international-algorithm-specific. Maps to credit risk (12.A), ML/DL (5.C), algorithmic modeling (13.B), and classification (6.A).

limitations: Data from a single institution limits cross-institutional applicability
Model fairness across demographic groups (gender, ethnicity) not evaluated
LSTM interpretability remains limited despite SHAP application
No catastrophic forgetting analysis for continuous model updating
Computational requirements exceed traditional scoring by 1.76×, which may be prohibitive for smaller lenders
remember_this: Hybrid LSTM + logistic regression achieves AUC 0.92 for credit default.
Type II error rate reduced to 7.8% (vs. 18.2% for logistic regression).
Credit history length and DTI ratio are the most predictive features (SHAP).
LSTM captures temporal patterns; logistic regression handles static features.
Optimal threshold at 0.32 via Youden's J for profit-maximizing classification.
